blocks.prompt: 9 (a) Find permutation of 10 people sitting on a bench if: There are no restriction.
blocks.explanation:
10 different people in 10 seats with no condition.
We must count the arrangements.
Plan: all 10 are arranged, so \(10!\).
steps:
Given: 10 people, 10 seats, no restriction.
To find: the number of arrangements.
Method: \({}^{10}P_{10} = 10!\).

Check
\[10! = 10 \times 9! = 10 \times 362880\]
\[= 3628800 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(9! = 362880\); a different route gives the same value.

blocks.prompt: 9 (b) Find permutation of 10 people sitting on a bench if: 3 cannot sit next to each other.
blocks.explanation:
3 particular people must not sit together as a group of three.
We must count the arrangements.
Plan: total \(-\) arrangements where the 3 sit together; "together" is counted by tying the 3 into one block.
steps:
Given: 10 people; 3 particular people must not all sit side by side.
To find: the number of arrangements.
Method: Not together = total \(-\) together. For "together", treat the 3 people as one block.
Note: this is how the book reads the condition (as in Example 6 and the answer key).

The 3 people together
\[\text{Units} = 1 + 7 = 8\]
\[\text{Ways} = 8! \times 3!\]
\[= 40320 \times 6 = 241920\]
Why: The block and the other 7 people are 8 units, arranged in \(8!\) ways; inside the block the 3 people can be arranged in \(3!\) ways.

Subtract
\[10! - 8! \times 3!\]
\[= 3628800 - 241920\]
\[= 3386880\]
Why: Removing the "together" arrangements leaves the ones where the 3 are not all together.

Another reading of the wording
If "no two of the 3 may sit next to each other" were meant, seat the other 7 first (\(7!\) ways); they make 8 gaps (ends included), and the 3 go into 3 different gaps in \({}^{8}P_{3}\) ways:
\[7! \times {}^{8}P_{3} = 5040 \times 336\]
\[= 1693440\]
Why: The answer key uses the first reading (3,386,880), so that is the expected answer.

Check with a small case
4 people with 3 not all together:
\[4! - 2! \times 3! = 24 - 12 = 12\]
Listing the 24 orders of A, B, C, D, exactly 12 have A, B, C in three neighbouring seats, so 12 do not \(\checkmark\)
Why: The method works on a case small enough to list.
